assumptions.name: September 2026 / May 2026 registered-birth ratio
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 (p49/p66 = 8,603) divided by May 2025 (p18/p64 = 8,433) gives 1.020. But 2026 is a Horse year with a steeper decline than 2025, and the 2025 September value was itself depressed by the 2024 Dragon-year base effect. The 2022 analogue (p37 = 12,217 September vs p36 = 12,242 October) suggests September is not systematically below May. A ratio centred near 1.26 with a wide range reflects the possibility that September 2026 is either close to the May 2026 level (6,832) or closer to the 2025 September level (8,603).
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the observed May 2026 level (p1) to September 2026, assuming the within-year seasonal shape is broadly stable between 2025 and 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Publication of June–August 2026 monthly birth counts showing a level far from the May 2026 value, or evidence that the 2026 seasonal shape differs materially from 2025.

p1.role: May 2026 registered live births in Taiwan (level anchor)

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent observed monthly level (May 2026, p1 = 6,832) and applies the 2025 September/May seasonal ratio (a1). This is the primary route because it uses the latest within-year level and a directly observed seasonal relationship. Shared dependency: both p1 and a1 rely on MOI monthly registration data; if the 2026 registration system changed, both are affected. Failure mode: the 2026 seasonal shape may differ from 2025, and May-to-September is a four-month extrapolation.

p49.role: September 2025 registered live births in Taiwan (same-month prior-year level)

methods.rationale: Uses the same calendar month in the prior year (September 2025, p49 = 8,603) and applies a y/y change factor (a2) consistent with the recent 2026 y/y declines. This is a standard seasonal-naive-with-trend route. Shared dependency: p49 and the 2026 y/y signal both come from MOI monthly releases. Failure mode: the y/y decline may accelerate or decelerate sharply, and September 2025 was already a low base.

p11.role: 2025 annual registered live births in Taiwan (annual level anchor)

a3.role: September share of 2026 annual registered births

methods.rationale: Decomposes the target as annual births times the September share. Uses the 2025 annual total (p11 = 107,812) as the level anchor and the 2025 September share (a3) as the seasonal factor. This route is less sensitive to month-to-month noise but assumes the 2026 annual total is near 2025 and that the seasonal share is stable. Shared dependency: p11 and a3 both derive from MOI annual/monthly data. Failure mode: the 2026 annual total may be materially below 2025, and the September share may shift.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / May 2026 registered-births ratio
assumptions.rationale: In 2025, September births (8,603, p49) were 1.020 times May births (8,433, p18). The 2026 monthly path is running below 2025 (Jan 8,723 vs 9,495; Feb 6,523 vs 10,407; May 6,832 vs 8,433), so the September/May ratio may differ from 2025. The range spans a continued decline (0.85) to a modest seasonal rebound (1.22), centered on the 2025 ratio.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 registration patterns follow the same seasonal shape as 2025 relative to May, with no major registration-timing shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 births are far below or above the May 2026 level by more than the stated range, e.g., a new record low or a policy-driven registration surge.

assumptions.name: September 2026 / September 2025 registered-births ratio
assumptions.rationale: The 2026 y/y decline has been running around 8-23% in Jan-Feb and about 19% in May (p1 vs p18). September 2025 was already a low base (8,603, p49). A ratio of 0.92 implies a further ~8% decline, consistent with the recent y/y pace but allowing for stabilization or a sharper drop.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 y/y decline in September is similar to the recent monthly y/y declines, with no major change in registration behavior.
assumptions.falsified_by: A September 2026 y/y decline outside the 0.78-1.08 range, e.g., a decline steeper than 22% or an outright increase.

assumptions.name: September share of 2026 annual registered births
assumptions.rationale: In 2025, September births (8,603, p49) were 7.98% of the annual total (107,812, p11). September is typically a mid-to-low month. The range allows for modest seasonal variation and for the 2026 annual total being uncertain.
assumptions.applies_when: The within-year seasonal distribution of births in 2026 is similar to 2025, and the 2026 annual total is near the central estimate.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 is a much larger or smaller share of the year than 7-9%, e.g., a policy-driven September surge or a data-reporting anomaly.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
